title: Monolithic hybrid quantum dot devices in superconducting twisted bilayer graphene
authors: Alexandra Mestre-Torà, Marta Perego, Clara Galante Agero, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Thomas Ihn, Klaus Ensslin, Artem O. Denisov
abstract: Gate-tunable superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG) has enabled the realization of superconducting devices, such as Josephson junctions, within a single crystal. This interface-free platform provides a reconfigurable and scalable architecture that overcomes limitations of conventional superconducting-semiconducting systems. Incorporating single-electron control enables access to regimes in which flat-band superconductivity competes with strong Coulomb repulsion, providing a platform for studying correlated physics phenomena. Here, we report a new class of quantum devices that combines electrostatic confinement with tunable superconductivity in a monolithic MATBG architecture. Within a single device, we demonstrate two complementary hybrid systems: superconducting islands and proximitized quantum dots. The superconducting island exhibits $2e$-periodic transport, indicating a well-defined gap protected against quasiparticle poisoning. The proximitized quantum dot hosts subgap Andreev states together with a strongly parity-modulated supercurrent.
summary: The research reports on monolithic quantum devices built using superconducting twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG). By combining electrostatic confinement with intrinsic superconductivity, the authors demonstrated distinct signatures of correlated physics, including $2e$-periodic transport in superconducting islands and parity-dependent subgap states in coupled quantum dots. This platform offers a highly tunable solid-state system for fundamental studies of strongly interacting electrons.
main_problem: To create a platform for studying strongly correlated physics by combining electrostatic confinement with tunable superconductivity within a monolithic, interface-free architecture.
main_result: The authors demonstrated robust $2e$-periodic transport in superconducting islands and observed even-odd parity modulation in subgap Andreev states within proximitized quantum dots on MATBG.
method: Transport measurements (conductance/resistance) were performed using four-probe techniques across varying gate voltages, magnetic fields, and temperatures.
model_or_system: The physical system is Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG), which hosts tunable superconductivity. The device integrates superconducting islands and quantum dots controlled electrostatically via finger gates.
key_observables: $2e$-periodic Coulomb oscillations, $1e$-periodic oscillations, subgap Andreev states, supercurrent modulation ($I_c$), and the transition between these periodicities based on external fields.

main_assumptions: The system is modeled using concepts from the Cooper-pair box approach for charge confinement, operating in regimes where $\Delta$ competes with $E_C$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate superconducting domes and insulating states across gate voltage maps; specific plots show the transition of Coulomb oscillation periodicity from $2e$-periodic to $1e$-periodic as a perpendicular magnetic field is applied.
paper_structure: The paper systematically characterizes the device by first mapping bulk phases (SC, BI, CI), then detailing single superconducting islands showing $2e$-periodicity, and finally analyzing proximitized quantum dots exhibiting parity-dependent subgap features and supercurrent modulation.
why_interesting: This work provides an experimental realization of tunable superconductivity coupled to strongly correlated electron physics in a 2D material platform, offering a clean system to study charge quantization effects beyond simple BCS superconductors.
